recipe.title: Dump-and-Go Crockpot BBQ Chicken Sweet Potatoes
recipe.summary: Pulled sweet-and-smoky BBQ chicken served over a crockpot sweet potato with tangy Greek-yogurt slaw for approximately 42 grams of protein and 380 calories.
recipe.story: The chicken and foil-wrapped sweet potatoes cook together all day. At night, shred the chicken and stir together a quick slaw while the crockpot keeps dinner warm.
recipe.serving_size: One 5-ounce sweet potato with approximately 6 ounces BBQ chicken and 3/4 cup slaw
ingredients: 2 pounds raw boneless skinless chicken breast
1 cup Ray's No Sugar Added Sweet & Smoky BBQ Sauce
1/2 cup Simple Truth Organic Chicken Bone Broth
6 small sweet potatoes, approximately 5 ounces each, scrubbed and dried
3/4 cup Chobani Nonfat Plain Greek Yogurt
instructions: In the morning, place the chicken breasts in the bottom of a 6-quart crockpot.
Pour the Ray's barbecue sauce and chicken bone broth over the chicken. Sprinkle with smoked paprika, granulated garlic, and onion powder.
Wrap each clean, dry sweet potato tightly in foil and arrange the packets above the chicken without pressing them into the sauce.
Cover and cook on LOW for 7 to 8 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F, shreds easily, and the sweet potatoes are tender when pierced.
At night, carefully remove the hot sweet potatoes and shred the chicken directly in the crockpot.
Stir the shredded chicken and contents of the crockpot together until evenly coated.
In a large bowl, stir together the Chobani Greek yogurt, apple cider vinegar, stevia, salt, and black pepper. Toss with the coleslaw mix.
Split one sweet potato per serving and top with approximately 6 ounces BBQ chicken and 3/4 cup slaw.
tips: Choose sweet potatoes close to 5 ounces each so they cook evenly and match the listed nutrition.
Keep the foil-wrapped potatoes on top of the chicken so they steam without sitting in the barbecue sauce.
Use Ray's No Sugar Added Sweet & Smoky sauce to keep the meal below 400 calories.
If the potatoes are much larger than 5 ounces, they may require more cooking time and will change the calories.
Nutrition is approximate and varies by chicken, sweet potato size, and product labels.
